results.query: What does Section 3(p) of the Patents Act say about traditional knowledge?

actual.answer_text: From the retrieved corpus: Section 3(p) - Traditional knowledge bar An invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge, or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of a traditionally known component or components, is not patentable. (The Patents Act, 1970, Section 3(p) - Traditional knowledge bar). 3(p): traditional knowledge or mere aggregation of known TK properties → not patentable. results.query: What does TRIPS cover for intellectual property protection?

actual.answer_text: From the retrieved corpus: What it is A WTO Agreement (1994) setting minimum global standards for IP protection and enforcement, binding on all WTO member states, including India. (Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), Overview - What it is). Article 39 - Protection of undisclosed information Members must protect undisclosed information (trade secrets) against unfair-competition-style misuse, provided it is (a) secret, (b) has commercial value because it is secret, and (c) has been subject to reasonable steps to keep it secret. (Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), Article 39 - Protection of undisclosed information). Members MAY also exclude: (a) diagnostic, therapeutic and surgical methods for treating humans or animals; (b) plants and animals (other than micro-organisms) and essentially biological processes for producing plants/animals (non-biological/microbiological processes must still be patentable) - BUT members must protect plant varieties either by patents, an effective sui generis system, or a combination (this is the TRIPS basis for India's PPV&FR Act, 2001). (Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), Article 27 - Patentable subject matter). This is legal information, not legal advice. Please verify with the relevant statute or a qualified legal/IP professional before acting.
